name: Corn Belt quarter on prairie loam
region: Des Moines Lobe, Midwest Corn Belt
headline: Some of the best soil on Earth, bare for six months a year while the heaviest rains of spring arrive.
story: An 80-acre rainfed field west of Ames in a corn-soybean rotation with fall tillage. Yields are excellent, but the soil is exposed from October to May, spring storms are getting heavier, tile lines carry nitrate to the river, and two crops in rotation invite rootworm and soybean cyst nematode.
challenge_tags: Bare soil in heavy spring rain

baseline_rotation.name: Corn - soybean, fall tillage
baseline_rotation.note: The Cropland Data Layer shows a strict corn-soybean alternation on this field since 2018.

water_context.in_situ_source: USGS NWIS streamflow, South Skunk River basin
water_context.note: Water quantity is rarely limiting. The issues are excess spring water, tile-drained nitrate, and occasional flash drought such as 2012 and 2023.

corn.note: Ethanol plants and feed mills within 30 miles.

soybean.note: Crush plants and river terminals bid strongly.

oats.note: Food-grade oat buyers contract in Iowa and Minnesota, but test weight specs are strict. Feed and straw are fallback outlets.

winter_wheat.note: Few elevators handle wheat; a river terminal or mill haul is likely.

alfalfa.note: Local hay demand from cattle and dairy; needs hay equipment or a custom operator.

triticale.note: Works if a neighbouring cattle operation buys or grazes it.
